comments.body:
Landed as Gerrit change 3111 (commit 47e431de04a, LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved, no advisories). make verify before the push: 17 failed, 19746 passed; all 17 failures are the known pandoc set under tests/unit/reconciler, none elsewhere, 0 ERROR lines.

Reproduction before the fix (2026-10-25, real git, two repos): origin/tickets held a commit the tracker lacked and the throttle marker was stamped 5 s ago. relation_snapshot.tracker_head_sha returned the tracker's old head, behind origin, and made no fetch.

Fix: ensure_fresh gains force, which skips only the 60 s age check; the opt-outs, the marker write and the swallow-every-failure contract are unchanged. force_fresh is threaded through tracker_head_sha, collect_plan_relation_snapshot and generation.collect, and set at the review-start snapshot and the pre-lock collect in sign_manifest only. The under-lock re-collect keeps the throttle, so nothing fetches while the lock is held.

Evidence on the merged tree (HEAD 47e431de04a), 2026-10-25 10:50 PDT:
- pytest tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py -q -> '40 passed in 108.52s'
- pytest tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py -q -k 'forced or sign_manifest or review_start' -> '7 passed in 7.92s'
All 7 of those new tests failed before the fix, each for the intended reason: TypeError on the missing force_fresh keyword, and the sign_manifest refusal test reached signing on a superseded description. They cover: forced head read fetches inside the window while the default does not; the sync.pull opt-out still blocks a forced read; a failing fetch is swallowed and the local head is returned; a forced snapshot pins the description edited on origin; sign_manifest raises PlanReviewGenerationChanged inside the window with one fetch; a forced retry fetches once per attempt (2 attempts, 2 fetches) and none under the lock; review start passes force_fresh=True.

Disposition: a forced fetch that fails is swallowed and review and signing continue on the local clone, as with the sync.pull opt-out. Unverified: end-to-end behavior on the deployed MCP server (two real clones); the tests use a two-repo fixture. Out of scope and ticketed as fabulous-avian-hoverfly: the claim-time currency check, which can still read a lagging clone.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The MCP server reviews plan material from its own tickets clone. An edit made in another
clone (local CLI or library) reaches that clone only through `reads.ensure_fresh`
(`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py`), a best-effort `git fetch` throttled to once per
60 s by a `/tmp/.ticket-sync-<md5>` marker. `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` (review start)
and the under-lock re-collect in `generation.sign_manifest` both go through that throttle.

So a review started, or signed, within 60 s of the server's previous fetch can pin a
description that is already superseded on `origin`. The under-lock re-check compares against
the same lagging clone, so it does not catch this. A claim through the same server inside the
same window would also see the lagging clone.

Split from next-embattled-geese (3b27-8f4b), which fixes the separate dedup-attach window.

## Evidence

- Code path read on origin/main 3beb7e4ad23: `tracker_head_sha` -> `ticket_reads.ensure_fresh`
  -> throttle check `marker_age < 60: return`.
- Not yet reproduced end to end; needs two clones sharing one origin.

## Reproduction (2026-10-25, host, real git, unit-test store of 2 repos)
`origin/tickets` holds a commit the tracker lacks; the shared throttle marker is stamped 5 s ago;
`relation_snapshot.tracker_head_sha(tracker)` then returns the tracker's old HEAD and performs no
fetch. Failing assertion: returned head != origin head. So the lag is real at the head-read seam.
Not yet shown end to end through `review_plan`/`sign_manifest` (the tests below do that).

## Approach (decided here)
Gate material reads force one fetch; every other read keeps the 60 s throttle.
1. `reads.ensure_fresh(tracker, *, no_sync=False, force=False)`: `force=True` skips only the marker
   age check. It still honors the opt-outs (`no_sync`, `sync.pull`, local-read context), still
   writes the marker, and stays best-effort (a fetch failure is swallowed).
2. `relation_snapshot.tracker_head_sha(..., force_fresh=False)` forwards it;
   `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(..., force_fresh=False)` and `generation.collect(...,
   force_fresh=False)` thread it. The default call shape is unchanged (existing fakes take one arg).
3. Pass `force_fresh=True` at exactly two places: the review-start snapshot in
   `plan_review/__init__.py` and the PRE-lock `collect` in `generation.sign_manifest`. The under-lock
   re-collect keeps the default, so no fetch ever runs while the signing/store lock is held: the
   pre-lock forced fetch has just stamped the marker, so the under-lock read is throttled.
4. A drift the pre-lock fetch reveals surfaces through the existing `fresh != initial_generation`
   check as `PlanReviewGenerationChanged` (re-review required), so no new refusal path is added.

Failure disposition: a forced fetch that fails (origin unreachable, no remote) is swallowed like every other freshness fetch, so review and signing proceed on the local clone. That
is the same outcome as the existing `sync.pull` opt-out and is required for environments with no
remote (portability); it is not retried and not an error. The fix removes the 60 s throttle lag,
not offline behavior.

Out of scope, each kept on the 60 s throttle on purpose: the claim-time currency check, `--status`,
every non-gate read, and the three other `collect` seams, which re-bind an already-produced verdict
to the clone's material and start no new review: the drift-refresh baseline
(`orchestrator.py`, only after `drift_refresh_candidate` finds a prior attestation), the attest
fallback collects (`attest.py`, only when no initial generation was passed), and the re-sign
baseline (`resign.py`). A fetch that races in after the pre-lock fetch and before the lock is still
possible; the window shrinks from up to 60 s to the lock-acquisition gap.

## Tests (tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py, reusing its `store` and `spy` fixtures)
- `tracker_head_sha(force_fresh=True)` inside the window fetches once and returns origin's head;
  the default call in the same state does not fetch (pins the unchanged default).
- A forced read still performs no fetch when `sync.pull` is off, and swallows a failing fetch.
- `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(force_fresh=True)` pins the description edited on origin; the
  default pins the older one.
- `sign_manifest` with an initial generation from the older description, origin edited since,
  marker fresh: raises `PlanReviewGenerationChanged`. A single-attempt call fetches exactly once,
  before the lock. Worked example for retries: with the first attempt forced into an under-lock
  mismatch, the call fetches once per attempt (2 attempts, 2 fetches) and the spy records no fetch
  while the lock is held.
- Review start (`review_plan`) calls the snapshot with `force_fresh=True`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A review started inside the throttle window pins the description currently on origin (test: snapshot with force vs default).
- [x] Signing refuses with `PlanReviewGenerationChanged` when origin's description changed since the review began, even with a fresh marker (test).
- [x] Each `sign_manifest` attempt performs at most one fetch, always before the lock and never while it is held; across retries the same per-attempt bound holds (test counts fetches per attempt, including a forced retry).
- [x] The default throttle and the opt-outs are unchanged for every other read (tests).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).

## Testing
```
pytest tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py -q
make verify
```
